system_overview: This specification models a basic append-only replicated log system. Multiple nodes share a single global log of transactions. Nodes can append new transactions to the log and independently execute (consume) transactions from it. The specification is part of a collection illustrating how ordinarily-infinite monotonic systems can be made finite for model checking.
actors_and_components: The system consists of a set of nodes and a set of possible transactions. The shared global log grows as nodes append transactions. Each node independently tracks how many transactions it has executed from the log. Nodes act both as writers (appending transactions) and as executors (processing transactions from the log).
state_variables: The system tracks two pieces of state: (1) a global ordered sequence of transactions representing the replicated log, and (2) a mapping from each node to a natural number indicating how many log entries that node has executed so far.
initial_state: The global log starts as an empty sequence. Each node's execution counter starts at zero, meaning no transactions have been executed.
actions: There are two types of transitions: (1) Write transaction: a node that has executed all current log entries (its execution count equals the log length) appends a new transaction to the end of the log and increments its own execution counter. This means only a fully caught-up node can write. (2) Execute transaction: a node that has not yet executed all log entries (its execution count is less than the log length) increments its execution counter by one, representing processing the next pending entry. The log itself is not modified during execution.
safety_properties: Each node's execution counter must never exceed the length of the log. In other words, no node can claim to have executed more transactions than currently exist in the log. Additionally, type correctness is maintained: the log remains a sequence of transactions and all execution counters remain natural numbers.
liveness_properties: Convergence: the system must repeatedly reach states where all nodes have executed every transaction in the log (all execution counters equal the log length).
model_bounds: The set of nodes and the set of possible transaction values are declared as constants. For model checking, these are instantiated as small finite sets (for example, three nodes and two transaction values).
additional_assumptions: Two alternative fairness specifications are provided, each sufficient to guarantee convergence: (1) Execute-fair: weak fairness on each node's execute action, combined with the assumption that eventually only execute actions occur (each node eventually stops writing). (2) Write-fair: weak fairness on each node's write action for each transaction, combined with the assumption that eventually only write actions occur. Both work because infinite suffixes of either action type imply convergence via the write action's enablement condition (a node must be caught up to write). The specification also defines several insufficiently fair and effectively false variants for illustration. The specification notes that with a single node, the execute action is never enabled because the writing node immediately increments its own counter.
